speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Notice of Motion.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Before I begin, Mr Speaker, I should mention that I am a little under the weather.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: My voice may not sound like its normal voice, a little raspier.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I will do my best to get through the speech in one go, without a break.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If you do need a break, just let me know.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It has been a remarkable journey, reflecting the grit and resilience of generations of Singaporeans in building our nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Sixty years ago, the world was very different.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It was the height of the Cold War, with the Berlin Wall standing as a stark symbol of division between the United States (US) and the Soviet Union.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In Asia, the Cold War spilled over into proxy fights, with devastating wars in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As a fledgling nation, Singapore faced monumental challenges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The withdrawal of British forces shortly after Independence dealt a heavy blow to our defence and our economy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In a world divided by blocs, we had no hinterland and no natural allies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yet in that crucible of fire, our pioneers forged a nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We refused to be pawns in someone else’s game.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We plugged into the world as an open and neutral hub for commerce and diplomacy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Together, we defined our relevance to the world and built this nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The stark divides of the Cold War have given way to a fragmented and troubled world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: New walls are being erected – not of concrete, but in the form of economic and trade barriers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And once again, we will have to find ways to navigate a turbulent external environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We bounced back strongly from the COVID-19 pandemic and ended last year on a strong footing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All this has given us good momentum for our next phase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we expect greater global uncertainty and downside risks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The US and China are locked in a fierce contest for global supremacy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But both know that economic heft and technological prowess are key to winning this global race.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And both are prepared to take more assertive actions to advance their own interests, even at the expense of established international norms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we can expect escalating attempts at containment and counter-containment, with ripple effects that will inevitably draw in other countries, including Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All these pressures will reshape the global economy and dampen prospects for global growth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As a small and open economy, we will feel the impact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For 2025, we expect a more moderate outlook.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But despite the uncertainties, we can look ahead with a degree of confidence.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore today is far stronger than we were 60 years ago.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have developed a strong and well-diversified economy, supported by a highly skilled workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have built up a robust Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and a strong diplomatic network, to uphold our sovereignty and security.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have forged a common Singaporean identity, grounded in our shared values and experiences, and our commitment to one another and our nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is the legacy of generations of Singaporeans, with each one running a good race.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The baton has now been passed and it is our turn to take Singapore forward.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This Budget builds on previous Budgets, not only to address today’s challenges, but to plan ahead and secure Singapore’s future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Budget 2025 is a Budget for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is also a Budget shaped together with all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It further advances our Forward Singapore agenda, which incorporates your aspirations and views, and seeks to keep our society strong and united.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In this Budget, we will work with you to: tackle cost pressures; advance our growth frontier; equip workers throughout life; build a sustainable city; nurture a caring and inclusive society; and rally as one united people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will go through each of these in turn.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Global inflation rose sharply in 2022, following the outbreak of the war in Ukraine and remained high after that due to energy, food and supply chain disruptions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we have been providing additional support measures over the last two years to cushion the impact on Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Package has helped to fully offset the effects of inflation for lower-income households and to provide a significant cushion for middle-income households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to provide support for as long as needed, within our means.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While inflation is expected to ease further this year, prices remain high.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singaporeans are still adjusting to these new price realities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some have had to tighten their belts, rethink spending habits, or make difficult trade-offs to manage their expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Therefore, in this Budget, I will provide additional support for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The first $500 will be disbursed in May this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the remaining $300 will be disbursed in January next year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As with previous CDC Vouchers, half can be used at participating supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the other half can be used at participating heartland merchants and hawkers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, I will provide additional U-Save rebates to help households cope with their utilities expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is double the amount of regular U-Save rebates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will cover about six months of utilities expenses for those living in 1- and 2-room flats, and three months of utilities expenses for those living in 3- and 4-room flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These credits are the same as the LifeSG credits we gave to National Servicemen last year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And parents can use them to defray their household expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can use this top-up to pay for their approved education-related expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More support will be extended to individuals and families who face greater financial stress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will increase the rates for the ComCare Assistance schemes, to better support lower-income households with basic living expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those supported by Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance will also receive more than before, based on the household’s composition, needs and income.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the monthly pension ceiling will also increase to $1,320.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through the ComCare Interim Assistance scheme, we will also provide more support for community organisations as well, to help households in need.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also paying close attention to public housing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have ramped up our Build-To-Order (BTO) supply decisively.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Application rates for BTO flats have stabilised and are now well below pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue with the robust supply pipeline.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the next three years, the Ministry of National Development (MND) will launch more than 50,000 new flats in a wide range of locations, including in Woodlands, Bayshore and Mount Pleasant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, more than eight in 10 first-timer families who collected keys to their BTO flats were able to service their monthly mortgage loans with little or zero out-of-pocket cash.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To put in perspective, this is a level of affordability that residents in other major cities like London, Sydney and Hong Kong do not enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we have been able to achieve this in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will continue to keep public housing affordable and accessible for all.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some Singaporeans prefer resale flats as they have shorter waiting times, but they are understandably concerned about the higher prices of resale flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our cooling and supply measures will eventually help to stabilise the resale market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Meanwhile, we will offer more options to home seekers who want their flats sooner.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This year, HDB will launch around 3,800 flats with a waiting time of less than three years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is about 20% of the full year’s BTO supply.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will continue to increase the supply of such flats in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB also launched the largest ever Sale of Balance Flats exercise last week, with around 5,500 flats available island-wide, and it plans to hold another balance flat exercise later this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Not all companies are profitable and some may not benefit from such a rebate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I will provide every active company that employed at least one local employee last year a minimum benefit of $2,000.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The total benefit that each company will receive will be capped at $40,000.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Despite facing higher cost pressures, I am glad that many businesses remain committed to uplifting the wages of lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The measures we have taken in recent years and are taking in this Budget, will help to mitigate the impact of rising costs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But in the longer term, the best way to adjust to higher prices is to grow the economy and increase productivity, so that all Singaporeans can enjoy higher real incomes and better standards of living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And let me turn to our strategies next in these areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will take bold and decisive actions to advance our growth frontier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Singapore economy now operates at a higher level.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And many other countries and cities are pressing ahead.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If we fail to stay competitive, we will be left behind.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must therefore redouble efforts to grow our economy and keep it dynamic and vibrant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Growth has a direct impact on the collective well-being of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, our economy grew by more than 4%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This meant higher wages and real incomes for many, many workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will be hard to achieve 4% growth on a sustained basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if we can secure an average of 2% to 3% growth per annum over the next decade, we will be able to create better jobs and opportunities, and improve standards of living for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To achieve this, we must continue to uphold several fundamentals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That includes: maintaining sound monetary and fiscal policies; harnessing market forces to drive efficiency and innovation; staying open to people and ideas to strengthen our capabilities; and deepening our tripartite partnership as a cornerstone of economic stability.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the same time, our approach and strategy must adapt to changing circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At this stage of development, we can no longer compete on cost alone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Instead, we must differentiate ourselves by producing high-value solutions for the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, we will enhance our technology and innovation engines.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is crucial because new ideas, innovation and technological progress are the drivers of growth.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We see this in the US, where the technology sector, powered by Silicon Valley and companies like Apple, Amazon, Alphabet and Tesla, has helped to propel the country’s dynamism and innovation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not operate at the same scale as the US.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we can still excel in specific areas of innovation and technology.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have a new generation of local tech companies like Grab, Sea and Razer, which have established themselves as regional or industry leaders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are home to the world’s top tech companies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They already have substantial activities here and are keen to do more out of Singapore, including in new frontier areas like artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Just as silicon chips fuel the tech industry, DNA chips are unlocking new frontiers in life sciences.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These chips enable scientists to sequence DNA, which can be used to diagnose diseases or identify patient risks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They demand high levels of precision engineering, to implant millions of DNA strands onto a glass or silicon surface.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, we are a key node for the broader life sciences sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also a major producer of advanced medical devices, including cardiac implants and hearing aids.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Take the example of American medtech company Illumina.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is the global leader in next-generation genetic sequencing instruments and DNA chips.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We serve as its Asia Pacific headquarters, and host a key research and development (R&D) and manufacturing site here.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Illumina’s genome sequencer is designed and manufactured in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Engineers across different disciplines worked together to design this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When COVID-19 first emerged, it was such a machine that first sequenced the virus.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It did so within hours, allowing scientists around the world to start developing drugs and vaccines.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Illumina’s presence has benefited other Singapore enterprises, like Venture Corporation and Sunningdale Tech.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Their partnerships with Illumina have helped them to build new innovation capabilities and expand to new areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To enhance our technology and innovation engines, we have to anchor more high-quality investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There have been attempts internationally through Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) 2.0 to ensure that multinational enterprises (MNEs) pay a minimum level of taxes worldwide, or to tilt the playing field in favour of governments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But in reality, MNEs wield considerable leverage and options.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why governments everywhere are still spending significant amounts to attract investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our R&D efforts are critical in powering our innovation and technology engines.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government has consistently invested about 1% of gross domestic product (GDP) annually in R&D over the last 20 years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, our biotech ecosystem would not be where it is today without Biopolis, which we built more than 20 years ago.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It also served as a platform for biotech talent to gather and share knowledge – knowledge that then diffused into our education system, which uplifted a new generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To sustain this momentum, we must invest to keep our R&D infrastructure at the cutting edge.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For our biotech sector, we will refresh our public biosciences and medtech research infrastructure in the greater one-north area.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will provide state-of-the-art facilities, promote collaboration within our research community and enable faster translation of research into commercial solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will provide industry-grade tools for researchers and industry partners to prototype and test new semi-conductor innovations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also support companies that undertake R&D and innovation in partnership with other stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have a good suite of schemes today, which we will further enhance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And more details are in the Annex to the Budget.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the years, we have developed a stronger pool of globally competitive startups and enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there is still more to be done.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want Singapore to be a place where exciting ventures develop and grow into the leading enterprises of the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We already have a good pipeline of such promising enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, AEM Holdings is a Singapore-headquartered provider of semi-conductor testing solutions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Its products serve a critical role in the chip production process, by helping to detect manufacturing defects or design flaws.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: AEM today has a global footprint, with manufacturing plants and R&D teams across Asia, Europe and the US.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide more support for enterprises to scale up, execute their growth plans and compete on the global stage.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In particular, I will extend our support schemes for internationalisation, and for mergers and acquisitions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And again, the details are in the Annex to the Budget.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some ventures are started by global companies, or by experienced entrepreneurs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To succeed, all enterprises must invest in technology to enhance their competitiveness and productivity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Enterprises can adopt off-the-shelf solutions like AI-powered analytics and digital marketing tools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to encourage the adoption of such solutions through initiatives like the Productivity Solutions Grant and the SMEs Go Digital.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond a certain stage, enterprises will need AI solutions, which are tailored to their needs and integrated into their business processes and systems.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Under this initiative, eligible enterprises will be partnered with major cloud service providers to access AI tools and computing power, as well as expert consultancy services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will help enterprises leverage AI more effectively in their transformation journey.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Companies also need capital to execute their growth plans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We now have a more vibrant financing ecosystem, backed by a growing network of angel investors, venture capitalists and private equity firms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is complemented by Government investment funds which invest in promising companies alongside commercial partners like 65 Equity Partners and Heliconia Capital.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Like other private equity funds, our investments generally span a three- to seven-year horizon.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To help enterprises with longer growth trajectories, we will deploy some of our funds as patient capital, with longer investment horizons, to ensure that promising companies have the resources they need to thrive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Globally, we have seen the emergence of a private credit market which offers innovative financing solutions to enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will provide more financing options for high-growth local enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the Minister for Trade and Industry will share more at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As enterprises scale up, they may also list on a stock exchange to access more capital.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Larger companies with significant overseas revenues will typically choose to list abroad to be closer to their main consumer markets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We recognise and accept these as commercial decisions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there has been feedback that the Singapore Stock Exchange is not attractive, even for companies that are focused mainly on Singapore and Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why we set up the Equities Market Review Group, chaired by Minister Chee Hong Tat, to strengthen the attractiveness of our stock market to such listings and investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Review Group has developed its first set of measures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will also introduce a tax incentive for fund managers which invest substantially in Singapore-listed equities, to encourage more investment in our capital markets.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Review Group will share more details on its measures in the coming days.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Third, to unlock our growth potential, we must invest in world-class infrastructure and find innovative ways to overcome our resource constraints.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore thrives as a hub economy, facilitating the flow of people, capital, goods and ideas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To sustain this position, we must ensure excellent connectivity with the rest of the world, both physically and digitally.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Development on the Tuas Port is progressing well, and Singapore recorded new highs last year in vessel arrival tonnage, container throughput and bunker sales.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This reinforces our role as a leading maritime hub.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have achieved island-wide 5G coverage and we are upgrading our Nationwide Broadband Network to deliver speeds up to 10 times faster.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will enhance digital connectivity for businesses and individuals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our air hub is another key pillar of connectivity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will break ground for Changi Airport Terminal 5 in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When completed, Terminal 5 will expand our airport’s capacity by more than 50% and will ensure that Singapore remains a critical gateway for global travel and trade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides infrastructure, we also need better solutions to address our resource constraints and enhance our economic resilience.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A generation ago, our critical constraint was water.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We tackled this head-on, developed NEWater and built our water industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The industries of the future – AI, semi-conductors, biopharmaceuticals – are highly energy-intensive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To meet these growing energy needs and to bring down our carbon emissions at the same time, we will need more clean power.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Expanding access to clean energy is therefore a major national imperative.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One immediate solution is to import low-carbon electricity from the region.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are making progress on such electricity imports.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have started a pilot with Peninsular Malaysia and expanded the capacity of a power trading initiative with Laos, Thailand and Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But beyond imports, we also need to have our own domestic sources of clean power to ensure greater energy resilience.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our options are inherently limited, because we do not have the natural resources nor the land to meet our needs using hydro, wind, or solar power.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been closely evaluating the use of low-carbon hydrogen for power generation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there are inherent challenges in the production, storage and transportation of hydrogen, which make it hard to scale up in a commercially viable manner.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One established low-carbon energy source that is used globally is nuclear power.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We had considered the possibility of using nuclear power back in 2010.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We assessed then that conventional nuclear technologies were not suitable for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we continued to keep a close eye on nuclear energy developments and progressively built capabilities in nuclear safety over the past decade to keep our options open.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Since then, we have seen significant advancements in nuclear technologies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One such development is that of small modular reactors (SMRs), which have better safety features than conventional reactors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Presently, only a few SMRs have been deployed around the world, but many more could become operational by the end of this decade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Interest in nuclear energy is also increasing worldwide.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In our region, several countries are planning to include nuclear in their energy mix.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also working on similar cooperation with other countries, which have capabilities and experience in civilian nuclear power, especially SMRs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Within the Government, we will re-organise ourselves to provide greater emphasis on this work.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will need new capabilities to evaluate options and to consider if there is a solution that Singapore can deploy in a safe and cost-effective way.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And these capabilities will also be needed for nuclear safety, which will become more salient given the growing regional interest in nuclear power.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Be it electricity imports, hydrogen or nuclear, we will need to make major investments in new infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our efforts to enhance our technology and innovation engines, strengthen our enterprise ecosystem, invest in new infrastructure and overcome our resource constraints, will enable us to refresh our value proposition and stay ahead in a rapidly changing world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the decades, we can see how Singapore’s economic success has translated to tangible improvements in our lives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the past, tertiary graduates had fewer job options to choose from, with career paths revolving around a few traditional areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These days, the job landscape is far more diverse.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those with an interest in science and engineering can pursue opportunities in advanced manufacturing, information technology (IT), biomedical science and sustainability, amongst others.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those with strengths in creativity and people-oriented roles can explore careers in the creative industry, lifestyle and hospitality sectors, as well as sports and fitness.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our thriving care economy also offers a wider range of opportunities, including in early childhood education, healthcare and elder care.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is what economic dynamism and growth can deliver for our people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And so, we will keep our economy strong and vibrant, and ensure that there are even more opportunities and good jobs for all Singaporeans – both now and in the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the jobs of the future will not be the same as the jobs of today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Rapid technological advances, especially in AI, will transform workplaces and jobs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Just a few years ago, tools like ChatGPT did not even exist.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now there is a rapidly expanding ecosystem of AI models.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can generate high-quality text, images and videos.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can write better programming code than many experts, assist in complex problem-solving and even help to accelerate research breakthroughs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: AI will get better in the future and other new disruptive technologies will emerge.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is hard to predict how they will impact specific industries and jobs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But one thing is clear: our workers must be equipped with the skills to stay competitive and relevant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we are investing heavily in lifelong learning and have made significant moves to strengthen SkillsFuture as a key pillar of our social compact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some Singaporeans prefer to continue working, while upskilling on a part-time basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Take, for example, Ms Zarina Binti Abdul Rahman.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She started out as an intern in Randstad Sourceright, a global recruitment agency, and is now an office administrator.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She wants to upgrade her skills in business operations, but is unable to pursue full-time studies due to her work and family commitments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, she is pursuing a part-time Diploma in Business Practice at Nanyang Polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this part-time training allowance will be implemented early next year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Education will share more at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also give a further boost to our lower-wage workers, who will benefit from early upskilling.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, our lower-wage workers can tap on the Workfare Skills Support Scheme from the age of 30.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The scheme provides employers with absentee payroll support when they sponsor workers for training.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It also provides workers with a training allowance when they go for self-sponsored training.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, the Workfare Skills Support Scheme is designed primarily to support short courses that are completed over a few days.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But lower-wage workers stand to benefit more from longer-form courses that provide more substantial reskilling and upskilling.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will therefore introduce an enhanced tier of support under the Workfare Skills Support for lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This enhanced support will be modelled after the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme and will benefit lower-wage workers when they turn 30.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this will start earlier, at age 30.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Manpower will share more details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our Institutes of Higher Learning are key partners in supporting lifelong learning.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They equip our workers with relevant skills for a changing economy, and provide a dedicated setting for deep learning.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will support the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) in developing a new city campus.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will enable SUSS to champion lifelong learning and deliver programmes with a strong social emphasis, at an accessible location in the city for learners of all ages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also extend the Singapore Universities Trust by 10 years to 31 March 2042 to support the fundraising efforts of our newer Autonomous Universities, namely SUSS and the Singapore Institute of Technology.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Trust provides matching grants for donations to support our Autonomous Universities in building up their endowment funds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We cannot stop the waves of technological innovations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we can and we will invest in every worker and every Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will equip everyone with the skills to adapt, compete and succeed in a changing economy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And in tandem, we will help our companies to restructure and transform, and to upgrade their workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Companies are best placed to drive business and workforce transformation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But some may face difficulties doing so due to short-term cost pressures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we have also received feedback and suggestions to streamline and improve the way Government agencies administer their support to enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will therefore introduce a new SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will bring together existing schemes administered by Workforce Singapore (WSG) and SkillsFuture Singapore, and simplify the application process.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The new grant will also provide higher funding support of up to 70% for job redesign activities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition, we will introduce a redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The credit is an existing scheme which helps employers defray the out-of-pocket costs for enterprise and workforce transformation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But to use the credit, companies have to pay upfront for staff training and then wait for reimbursement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And there are also employers who are not aware of the credit or how it can be used.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will redesign the credit to make it more accessible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The revamped credit will operate more like an online wallet.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Companies can easily check how much they have.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And they can use the credits to immediately offset out-of-pocket costs for eligible workforce transformation initiatives and courses, rather than do so on a reimbursement basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All companies with at least three resident employees will get a fresh $10,000 in the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise credit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The new credit will be available in the second half of 2026 and will last for three years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our tripartite partners play key roles in workforce transformation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In particular, the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC’s) Company Training Committees (CTCs) bring union leaders and employers together to design and implement workforce upgrading plans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Since the initiative started in 2019, NTUC has set up more than 2,700 CTCs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Almost four in five are in small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through the NTUC’s CTC grant, NTUC is supporting more than 400 transformation projects, which will benefit over 7,000 workers with better work prospects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Take for example SATS, our main air cargo handler and airline caterer at Changi Airport.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: SATS is investing in new equipment and technology to improve the efficiency of its catering services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It also needs to train its workers to handle the new equipment, and redesign workflows and jobs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It can access the additional $10,000 in SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It can tap on the new SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant to cover up to 90% of the cost for reskilling workers, and up to 70% of the cost for redesigning jobs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: SATS has worked with NTUC to form a CTC and has been sending its employees for the Work-Study Diploma in Airport Operations at the Institute of Technical Education (ITE).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Work-Study Diploma helps these employees acquire critical skills, including managing operations and resource planning.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And they can go on to take on supervisory roles in SATS, subject to good performance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, SATS fully sponsors its workers’ out-of-pocket programme fees.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The CTC grant will help to offset some of these training costs and provide enhanced funding for absentee payroll when the trainee is away from work.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, these are tangible benefits that companies can enjoy and we encourage all companies to press on with their workforce and business transformation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition to broader workforce transformation, we will strengthen our support to nurture and groom Singaporean leaders in the corporate sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More and more Singaporeans are taking on leadership roles in large firms and MNEs operating here.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide more support to equip Singaporeans and enable them to succeed on their own merit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To compete for leadership roles with regional and global responsibilities, Singaporeans must gain overseas experience – managing operations in different countries, navigating diverse cultures and working seamlessly across borders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, Government agencies like Enterprise Singapore, the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Infocomm Media Development Authority have schemes which support companies to send Singaporeans for overseas work postings and leadership milestone programmes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The feedback from such schemes has been positive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will set aside more resources to increase the capacity of these schemes and provide more opportunities for promising Singaporean leaders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the Minister for Manpower will share more at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even with reskilling and upskilling, some workers may face career setbacks due to economic and business disruptions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will help workers who lose their jobs to get back on their feet through the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme, which will start from April this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also increase the provision of career matching services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, WSG and its partners, like NTUC’s e2i, run about 30 centres and touchpoints island-wide, placing about 40,000 jobseekers every year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The centres work with the jobseekers to shortlist jobs, work on their resumes and prepare them for interviews.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides nation-wide programmes, there is benefit in facilitating job search at a localised level.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will help jobseekers who prefer to take on jobs near their homes, for example, to balance work and caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, North East CDC runs Job Placement Centres for its district, in partnership with WSG.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will expand localised job matching to all CDCs across the island.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also strengthen our support for two groups of workers in this Budget – seniors and ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More seniors are staying employed as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to work with employers to tap on the experience and wisdom of seniors who are able and wish to continue working.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will provide wage offsets for employers who hire Singaporean seniors aged 60 and above, and earning less than $4,000 a month.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government will reimburse companies up to 7% of the wages that they pay to workers aged 69 and above.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Later this year, the Ministry of Manpower will convene a Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The workgroup will undertake a holistic and longer-term review of senior employment policies, to improve the employability of seniors and increase the availability of jobs that better suit their needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With this move, senior workers can build up their retirement savings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And businesses will get continued support from the Government to cushion the impact on business cost.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For ex-offenders, employment is integral to their re-integration into society.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To encourage employers to give ex-offenders a second chance, we had earlier introduced the Uplifting Employment Credit, which provides a wage offset to employers hiring ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, the credit supported close to 700 employers in hiring more than 1,500 ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will do everything we can to develop and realise the potential of all our people, so that they, in turn, realise their aspirations and dreams for themselves and their families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our Singapore Story is one of sustained investment and continuous improvement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over time, we have transformed our living environment into a thriving metropolis and a beautiful home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is still much more to do in the years ahead.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will: upgrade our homes and estates; refresh and rejuvenate our landscape and infrastructure; and importantly, prepare for a future of rising global temperatures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Addressing the climate crisis requires strong international collaboration and collective action.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Unfortunately, momentum on global climate efforts has slowed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will make it harder for all of us to tackle climate change.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Despite these challenges, we remain resolute in our commitment to decarbonisation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will work with international partners and do our part to sustain efforts and drive meaningful progress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will bring us one step closer to realising our longer-term aim of achieving net zero emissions by 2050.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I shared earlier about our plans to access more sources of clean power.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That will be critical for us to achieve net zero.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond energy, we will also accelerate efforts to decarbonise our transport sector, which accounts for about 15% of our total emissions today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our aim is to have 100% cleaner energy vehicles by 2040 and we are making good progress towards this target.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, around a third of all new cars registered were Electric Vehicles (EVs) and almost half were hybrid vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But adoption of clean energy variants of heavy vehicles has been slower, due to limited model availability, higher upfront costs and less accessible charging infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To accelerate the adoption of clean heavy vehicles, we will introduce a new Heavy Vehicle Zero Emissions Scheme and an Electric Heavy Vehicle Charger Grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These schemes will provide incentives for the purchase of a heavy vehicle, and co-funding of the charging infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Transport will share more at COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, drivers of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles pay fuel excise duties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These duties contribute to revenue and also serve as a form of usage charge.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: EVs, while much less pollutive, should not be exempted from usage charges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are still considering how to design a usage-charge mechanism for cleaner energy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the interim, we have introduced the Additional Flat Component (AFC) of road tax, for cars and electric light goods vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will now introduce the AFC for electric heavy goods vehicles and buses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will be phased in over three years starting from January 2026 and will be implemented in full by January 2028.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Alongside electrification, increasing the use of mass public transport is central to reducing emissions and our vision of a more connected and car-lite Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singaporeans can look forward to the new Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line, as well as the extensions of the Thomson-East Coast Line, Downtown Line and the Circle Line.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to study how our rail network can be expanded.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we are also investing close to an additional $1 billion to increase and enhance our bus services under the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As we do our part to reduce emissions in Singapore, we also have to assume the worst and take steps to protect ourselves against climate risks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If the world continues on a fossil fuel-based development trajectory over the coming years, global temperatures will keep rising and that means we can expect a mean sea level rise of over one metre by 2100.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Coupled with high tides and storm surges, the impact will be significant, well above one metre, and that means that around one-third of Singapore will be vulnerable to coastal flooding.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are therefore developing and implementing plans to better protect our island.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will employ a range of solutions to do so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These range from static structures like sea walls, to more specialised measures like barrages and tidal gates, as well as reclamation to create more land.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the southeastern part of Singapore, we earlier announced plans to reclaim land to develop “Long Island”.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides raising the ground level above rising sea levels, this will create additional space for homes, as well as new waterfront parks for outdoor recreation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition, PUB will complete site-specific studies for the Greater Southern Waterfront and Changi this year; studies for Jurong Island and the Northwest Coast are also underway.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And step by step, we will complete the plans for coastal protection around the entire island.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The actual implementation of measures could stretch over two decades or longer, starting from the 2030s onwards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government is taking steps to green our energy and transport sectors and to protect our island from climate risks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singaporeans too, have a part to play in this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Individuals have the power to drive change through their choices and behaviour.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To fully realise our green future, we will need to make lifestyle adjustments and adopt sustainable habits in our daily lives.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I encourage all households to make the switch to more resource-efficient products if you have not done so already.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have come a long way in building today’s Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our next decade will be pivotal, as we accelerate efforts to decarbonise our economy, and enhance the climate resilience of our built environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as long as this Government is in charge, we are committed to delivering them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will ensure that our island nation survives even as the oceans rise and we will build a better and greener future for all.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A major part of our Forward Singapore agenda is to nurture a more caring and inclusive society – one where every Singaporean feels valued and supported, regardless of age, ability and circumstance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And in this year’s Budget, I will take further steps towards these goals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Families play a key role in strengthening our society and supporting each of us to be the best version of ourselves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will do more to support their efforts to achieve stability, self-reliance and mobility.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Under this initiative, we are providing more customised support.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Family coaches and volunteer befrienders work directly with ComLink+ families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Together, they develop concrete action plans to achieve nearer- and longer-term goals, like obtaining employment and saving for a home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As the families make progress, they will receive financial top-ups in the form of ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In tandem with ComLink+, we have the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It helps second-timer families with children living in public rental flats to start afresh and own their own homes by buying a shorter-lease new flat with an additional housing grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are also first-timer families with children living in public rental flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They typically face more significant challenges in life, like coping with medical issues in the family, or raising children as a single parent.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Hence, they may have difficulties buying a flat with a full 99-year lease, even as first-timers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To support these families in their home ownership journey, we will allow them to buy shorter-lease subsidised flats through Fresh Start.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the Minister for National Development will share more at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While we provide targeted help for the more vulnerable groups, we will also do more to support all families across every stage of life.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have made significant moves in recent years, including enhancing the Baby Bonus Cash Gift and the Government’s contributions to the Child Development Account (CDA).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have just enhanced paid parental leave to 30 weeks in total, which will enable parents to spend more time with their infants.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In this Budget, we will further reduce monthly full-day childcare fee caps in Government-supported preschools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: After basic childcare subsidies, a dual-income family will pay about $300 per child.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Lower- and middle-income families will pay less after additional subsidies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this reduction will keep full-day preschool expenses similar to those of the fees for primary school and after-school student care combined.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will apply to each third and subsequent child born from today onwards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The CDA monies can be used to defray preschool and healthcare expenses of the child and their siblings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will be disbursed into the mother’s MediSave account again for each third and subsequent child born from today onwards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this can be used to offset the mother’s pregnancy and delivery costs, or her family members’ healthcare expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this can help to defray a wide range of household expenses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They have four children, turning one, four, seven and eight this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will receive $500 in LifeSG credits for each child.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is to help them with cost pressures, which I had highlighted earlier in my speech.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will also receive $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG credits for each of their third and fourth children, up to when they turn six.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That amounts to $11,000 in benefits from this Budget.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Joel and Kristen have two daughters turning three and five this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They are expecting a baby boy in May.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, they will receive the one-off $500 in LifeSG credits for each of their children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But with a third child on the way, they will receive the full benefits of the Large Families Scheme – $5,000 in CDA, $5,000 in MediSave and $1,000 every year until the child is six years old.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, as a family, they will receive a total of $17,500.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Seniors are an important part of many families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To support our seniors to live and age well, we have been reviewing and updating our approach to retirement, healthcare and caregiving.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have provided seniors more assurance for their retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We introduced the Majulah Package, to support all seniors born in 1973 or earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we also enhanced the Workfare Income Supplement and the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our priority is to empower our seniors to stay active and healthy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why we rolled out Healthier SG and Age Well SG.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our plans include creating a more conducive living environment for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme, we have significantly improved the mobility and safety of seniors through subsidised senior-friendly fittings and installations in HDB households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will expand EASE for three years up to 2028 to households living in private properties, so that more seniors can benefit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As we get older, we are all likely to spend more on healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The scheme will be made available to eligible lower-income seniors aged 55 to 70 years old.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For every dollar of voluntary top-ups received in their MediSave accounts, the Government will provide a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $1,000 per year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this will complement the existing Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Both matched savings schemes will help lower-income seniors, especially our grandmothers, mothers and aunts who were homemakers and caregivers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The contributions from the Government and their loved ones will better support their retirement and healthcare needs, and give them greater assurance as they age.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While we will do our best to help our seniors stay healthy, the reality is that over time more of them will become frail and may require long-term care.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, the Government provides significant subsidies for long-term care services, particularly for lower- and middle-income families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is complemented by CareShield Life, which is our national long-term care insurance scheme, which provides a monthly cash payout upon severe disability.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also raise the maximum qualifying per capita household income to $4,800.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many in the older cohorts, especially those born in 1969 or earlier, do not benefit from CareShield Life and therefore will face higher out-of-pocket costs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For this group, we will introduce additional subsidies of five percentage points.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many seniors prefer to age in place as much as possible, supported by their families and friends.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can opt for a range of care options.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some may use care services like day care or home care, while others rely primarily on family caregiving.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also enhance support across the entire spectrum.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will increase existing subsidies for long-term care services in the home and community by up to 10 percentage points and similarly raise the maximum qualifying per capita household income to $4,800.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will similarly introduce additional subsidies for cohorts born in 1969 and earlier by 15 percentage points.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also increase the subsidies provided under the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund to cover the rising costs of home healthcare items, like adult diapers, and to also cover additional categories of such items.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To better support those who are looking after seniors at home, we will enhance the Home Caregiving Grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a cash grant which can be used to offset daily care costs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will raise the quantum for the Home Caregiving Grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides higher subsidies, insurance will also play a part in easing the cost burden of long-term care.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With a rapidly ageing population, we have to work hard to manage the increase in long-term care costs, and ensure a good mix of funding support between individual co-payment, government subsidies and insurance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are studying this issue carefully, and the Minister for Health will say more at COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also do more to support persons with disabilities and ensure they can live with dignity and pursue their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have laid good foundations with our investments in Early Intervention and Special Education, which support persons with disabilities until they are around 18.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But many parents worry about what happens post-18, after their children graduate from the structured environment of a Special Education (SPED) school.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are looking into these post-18 pathways for these students and studying how we can provide more meaningful support.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In particular, those who are transiting to work may need more support to build up their work readiness and adjust to an employment setting.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This includes additional learning support to gain soft skills and to adapt to new routines.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: After graduating from Saint Andrew’s Autism School in 2021, she underwent three months of employment training in housekeeping and soft skills.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She was able to secure a nine-month internship with the Lee Ah Mooi Old Age Home as a General Housekeeping Assistant, under supportive supervisors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the end of the internship, she was offered full-time employment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And she is now doing well at this Home and happy to do her part to take care of the residents there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to see more stories like her.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And so, we will invest more in building the support structures for persons with disabilities to transit more smoothly from school to work.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also do more for those with higher care needs, who need a more structured environment beyond school to stay active.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are issues which we will study comprehensively with stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will be a multi-year endeavour and the Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister for Education will share more at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Concurrently, we will provide more support for employers, who may be concerned about the costs and effort needed to redesign jobs and adapt their workplaces when they hire people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also provide more financial support to persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Their caregivers may benefit from the increase in the Home Caregiving Grant which I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As with the enhancements for seniors, we will increase subsidy rates for adult disability services and raise the maximum qualifying per capita household income for these subsidies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will expand the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to include eligible Singaporeans with disabilities regardless of their age, to help them save for retirement early.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also step up efforts by SG Enable and the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) to encourage families to plan ahead for their child’s future care needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, caregivers can set up financial care plans and set aside monies in trust accounts with SNTC, which will manage the trust monies for the person with disability when their caregivers pass on.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In this Budget, I have focused on families, seniors and their long-term care needs, and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we will continue to review and update other policy areas over time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because we want to build a Singapore where we have each other’s backs, where no one is left behind and where we continue to stay strong and united as one people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singaporeans across different generations and from all walks of life have played a vital role in getting us to SG60.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For a country, 60 years is a short time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we have made great strides over this period and there is much to be grateful for.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In this Budget, I will introduce an SG60 package to recognise the contributions of all Singaporeans and to share the benefits of our nation's progress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, I will give SG60 Vouchers to all Singaporeans aged 21 and above this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Each one will receive $600 in SG60 Vouchers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singaporean seniors aged 60 and above will receive $200 more – so, $800 in vouchers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can be used at all businesses that accept CDC Vouchers – and half can be spent at participating supermarkets and the other half at participating heartland merchants and hawkers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will disburse the SG60 Vouchers across the month of July.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Seniors will claim first, and the rest later.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The People’s Association and the CDCs will share more details later.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Third, as Minister Indranee had announced earlier, we will welcome all Singapore Citizen babies born this year with an SG60 Baby Gift.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our unity is a precious asset, which we must never take for granted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The experiences of countries around the world show how easy it is for trust to be eroded, and for societies to become deeply divided and polarised.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must therefore remain steadfast in nurturing our cohesion and unity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And in this Budget, we will invest more in strengthening our cultural core and our community bonds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will introduce an SG Culture Pass, to encourage Singaporeans to attend arts and heritage activities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The credits will be made available from September this year and are valid until the end of 2028.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth will share more about upcoming initiatives for the arts and heritage sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our hawker centres and markets are an integral part of our way of life.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This year marks over half a century since we built our first hawker centres and markets, and the fifth anniversary of the inscription of our Hawker Culture onto the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will serve the changing needs of our stallholders and patrons.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Sports is another avenue for Singaporeans of all races, religions and backgrounds to come together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, we cheered on Team Singapore at the Olympics and Paralympics, rejoicing as our flag was raised high.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We celebrate with them when they do well and we encourage them when they face setbacks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are building new facilities in our heartlands, so that Singaporeans can enjoy sports closer to where they live.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the coming years, we will have new sports facilities in Toa Payoh, Punggol and Clementi.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we are also upgrading existing facilities in Pasir Ris, Queenstown and Hougang.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide $100 in SG60 ActiveSG credits for all ActiveSG members to enjoy sports together with their family and friends.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: You can sign up for the free membership at the ActiveSG website and can use these credits to book ActiveSG facilities and programmes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our solidarity has seen us through many challenges, including our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must continue to help our fellow citizens and ensure we move forward together, as a people and a nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To encourage this spirit of giving, the Government provides matching funds that multiply the impact of donations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government and Tote Board now provide dollar-for-dollar matching grants for the fund-raising projects of Singapore-registered charities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide a $270 million top-up to this Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme, which will be extended for three years until the end of FY2027.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many Singaporeans are passionate about social causes but may not have a specific charity in mind.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And to encourage sustained giving amongst larger donors, we will provide a higher $1.50 in matching for donations with a minimum three-year commitment of at least $250,000 per year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In total, the Government and Tote Board will set aside more than $600 million in matching funds to strengthen our spirit of giving.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Earlier, I had shared about the SG60 Vouchers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those who are better off may want to donate their vouchers to those with greater needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will facilitate this and we will share more on how to do so in due course.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our self-help groups play an important role in addressing the needs of their respective communities and in strengthening our social compact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide the self-help groups with additional funding of $60 million over the next five years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will enable them to enhance their programmes and better support their communities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many businesses have also stepped forward to support their fellow Singaporeans in this SG60 year, and will be providing special SG60 discounts and offers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore is at its strongest when we stand together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we are all Singaporeans, living on this tiny red dot, as one family.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we rally together as one, there is no challenge we cannot overcome.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this unity is what keeps us resilient, thriving and moving forward, even in an uncertain and troubled world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A critical enabler for Singapore’s continued success is sound and healthy public finances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We achieve this by living within our means and running a balanced budget over each term of government.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means spending prudently to meet our immediate and future needs, ensuring that our revenues cover expenditures and keeping the tax burden as low as we can, while not burdening Singaporeans with debt.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In this term of government, we have made several significant changes to our tax system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These revenue moves give us the resources we need to meet our spending needs and also make our fiscal system more progressive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through the Assurance Package, we have cushioned and delayed the impact of the GST increase for the majority of Singaporean households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Importantly, we have designed our GST system with permanent GST vouchers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This ensures that lower-income households pay a far lower effective GST rate than higher-income households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also continue to ensure fairness and improve progressivity in our tax system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means that those who are better off will pay more in taxes to help their fellow citizens.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we raised Property Tax rates for all non-owner-occupied residential properties, which are mainly investment properties, as well as for higher-value owner-occupied residential properties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Property Tax rate changes coincided with a sharp increase in the Annual Values of properties, which arose because of COVID-19-related supply constraints in the property market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have therefore revised and updated the Annual Value bands of owner-occupier Property Tax rates for residential properties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that means that more homes now fall within bands with lower tax rates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To further cushion the impact, we provided Property Tax rebates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Taken together, all HDB owner-occupiers and over 90% of private residential property owner-occupiers will see lower Property Taxes this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The changes we made to our tax system this term have put us on a stronger fiscal footing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They provide us the resources we need to better meet our society’s needs – all while keeping our overall system of taxes and transfers fair and progressive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For FY2024, our revenue collections were better than expected.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A key reason is the upside in our Corporate Income Tax.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Corporate Income Tax is now the single largest contributor to total revenue – larger than even the Net Investment Returns Contribution.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are several reasons for this higher Corporate Income Tax collection.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Part of it is due to industry-specific cyclical factors, for example, in finance and wholesale trade.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It could also be due to changes in the investment decisions of multinational enterprises, as they seek out stable and reliable centres like Singapore to put more of their high-end activities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While our revenues have increased, we have also spent more on Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, we provided $3 billion in MediSave top-ups in December last year, which will help to cushion the increase in MediShield Life premiums to fund better coverage and higher payouts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also earmarked resources for projects to boost economic competitiveness, including developing critical infrastructure like Changi Terminal 5, and for the energy transition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to keep an eye on our medium-term fiscal projections.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In 2023, MOF released an Occasional Paper showing that we expect to keep our fiscal position roughly balanced until 2030.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is still considerable uncertainty about how Government revenues will unfold over the coming decades.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But how much revenue we will get from this change depends on whether these MNEs continue to find it attractive to remain in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Moreover, there is now great uncertainty about the global tax environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The new US administration has withdrawn from the earlier consensus forged by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and other countries.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And it remains to be seen what further moves the US and other major economies will make in this new geopolitical environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will assess our options as global tax developments unfold and adjust our policies where necessary.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Meanwhile, we are certain that expenditure will continue to rise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Government spending has been rising steadily over the years from about 15% of GDP to about 18%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And based on historical trends, we can expect our spending to go up to 20% of GDP by around 2030.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With growing global uncertainties, the need to invest more in our workers and better support our rapidly ageing population, there will be added pressure to raise spending – possibly at a pace that exceeds previous increases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will continue to monitor fiscal trends closely and update our medium-term projections.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ultimately, we will always ensure that all Singaporeans benefit from our nation’s progress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, in this SG60 year, we will complete one cycle, and we will enter a new phase of nation-building.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must brace ourselves for new challenges in this next phase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The world is in turmoil and the situation is likely to get worse in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But this is not the first time that Singapore has had to confront tough external circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have done so repeatedly over the last six decades and so, we can draw confidence from what we have been through together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Like Mr Yau Jon Kiang, who is 75 this year and a resident in Yew Tee.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In our early years of nation-building, he and his wife worked long hours in a canteen at the Tanjong Gul Camp at Tuas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They put food on the table for the SAF, as well as their own young sons at home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Their never-say-die spirit lives on in the family.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Jon Kiang’s son, Joses, forged his own path to become a naval engineer with the SAF.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He endured long stints at sea to serve and defend our nation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Determined to improve his family’s future, he pursued part-time studies and earned an engineering degree, while juggling work and family responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: His children are now entering adulthood, at 17 and 22.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They have grown up in a more affluent Singapore, but they too face their share of challenges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: His daughter Jamie started at Singapore Polytechnic just as the COVID-19 pandemic hit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Her school went online, and her daily activities were disrupted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But she did not let that get her down.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She adapted and pushed forward, just as her father and grandfather had done before her.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I met Jamie and some of her fellow youth leaders back in 2022, after we had battled COVID-19 for two and a half years; they were optimistic, resilient and full of ideas about how they can contribute.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Since then, Jamie has graduated from Singapore Polytechnic as Valedictorian.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, she is pursuing her Bachelor’s in Integrative Studies at Singapore Management University, while leading a non-profit to empower and support youths in tech.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: She hopes to work in the philanthropic sector to make a greater impact after graduation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is what the Singapore spirit is about.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At every turn, we have chosen determination over despair, innovation over stagnation, and solidarity over division.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Every generation has carved a path through its challenges and paved the way for the next generation to go even further.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The road ahead will not be without challenges, but I am confident that our best days lie ahead of us.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Together, we can keep Singapore an evergreen oasis of stability, hope, and opportunity for all.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let us move onward together for a better tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Debate to be resumed on what day, Prime Minister?
